㊥ (both consequences) Both are under way. kimi-3 is making the new frame appear the moment you press RET, built from 小象's draft without a stepper reload. 大象, the classical reader of agent turns, is now written into E-agency-work-orders (`cbfeeeba`) as the step that runs before the logic. kimi-1's job that's already running is its first part.

㊯ (frame at RET, kimi-3) Job `invoke-…-66163820`, park `park-a5306a1a-…`.
- **The JVM drafts inline** when you send, bounded at 2 s, and returns the draft with its answer. If a draft is slow (the 11 s case was probably a model rebuild), it falls back to drafting in the background as now.
- **Emacs passes the draft to the stepper,** which builds frame 311 in Elisp from your turn and the draft, with no `turn_frames.py` run. It moves you there only if you were on the last frame. When 象's reading lands, the full reload replaces the frame in place.
- **A test pins the Elisp-built frame** to exactly what `turn_frames.py` would produce for the same turn, so the two can't drift apart.

🈖 (大象) 象 stays off agent text. 大象 reads each agent turn classically when it ends, well under a second, and turns it into acts. Only then does the kernel judge what closed and what's open. That's McCarthy's speech acts, as in Elephant 2000 (fitting for an elephant), over Fong's open ports. Its inputs are all things Agency already holds when the turn ends:
- the reply's marks and their bracketed targets;
- the bells the agent sent during the job, which are its work orders;
- the parks it set;
- its commits, through the signing trailers;
- ownership claims like "I own" or "will replay", read by fixed patterns and kept only when they name a next step.

Acts get stable ids, so reading a turn twice gives the same acts.

㊢ (how the pieces fit)
- **kimi-1's adapter (running):** covers 大象's marks and commits, plus your side from 象's readings.
- **kimi-2's ledger, W1 (running):** records the bells as work orders.
- **Later:** parks and claims are the remaining 大象 inputs.
- **W3 (after W1):** connects the token check to job end. When 大象's acts come in, the same check reads from the kernel, so the HUD and the nudges judge open/closed the same way.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the token system) Understood, no watcher. I've designed a work-order (token) system for Agency, aimed at the codex-18/19/20 case, and two parts of it are being built now. Each delegated piece of work becomes a token that some agent always holds. When an agent's job ends while it still holds a token and nothing else is moving it, Agency nudges that agent once to either dispatch the next step or close the order. If that doesn't move it, Agency escalates. It runs on job ends, not a timer.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (how the stasis happens) codex-19 sends codex-20 work to implement and codex-18 work to replay, and each result comes back to codex-19 by auto-bellback. codex-19 then writes something like "handoff closed, codex-18 will replay", and its turn ends. If that turn dispatched nothing, all three sit idle, and nothing records that codex-19 still owes the next step. Right now codex-19 and codex-20 are both running, so it's moving at the moment.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the design, `6819c30d` in E-agency-work-orders)
- **Open.** A work bell opens an order owed by the recipient, under the order the sender is working on. An agent's first work bell also opens a root order on the agent itself, owed to you. In this case that root is codex-19's mfuton chain.
- **Deliver.** When the recipient's job ends, the token goes back to the requester. When the requester's turn handling the result ends, the order closes.
- **Check.** The check runs when a job ends. If that agent owes an order, nothing below it is open, and it has no running job, queued job or park, it gets one nudge naming the order and the choice it owes. A second idle job end escalates to the requester, or to you for a root. After that it stops, so there's no reminder storm.
- **Kernel.** Each step is also written as a P24 act, so the kernel and the HUD read the same orders.
